ios.desc:
HNowledge is a personal archive of all the stories and comments on Hacker News you've upvoted. Sign in with your existing Hacker News account and the app pulls in everything you've ever upvoted and stores it locally on your phone.

FEATURES

- Reads the stories and comments you upvoted into a local archive
- Add a private note to anything, and tag it however you like
- Search through all upvoted titles, comments, and notes
- Filter your upvotes by tag, date, or story type and group them by domain, authors, or month
- Read an upvoted comment in its context right from the app, or navigate to the full thread
- Select any profile and see all their stories and comments you upvoted
- Fully offline: once upvotes are synced, the archive stays on your device
- Export your whole archive as JSON at any time

Please note: this is a read-only archive, not a full Hacker News client. You cannot upvote, submit or comment on any content on Hacker News using this app, and it is not a front-page reader either: it shows what you already upvoted, not what's new.

YOUR ARCHIVE, ON YOUR DEVICE

There is no HNowledge account and no HNowledge server. Your Hacker News login goes to Hacker News and nowhere else, stored in the iOS Keychain. The archive lives entirely on your device and nothing is ever uploaded, analysed, or shared.

HNowledge is an unofficial client and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Hacker News or Y Combinator.

Stories and comments come from Hacker News:
https://news.ycombinator.com/
https://github.com/HackerNews/API

quotes.text:
Noticed how well Claude works for transcribing old German cursive, especially for broad hits in non-indexed 17th century parish records. Motivated me to pick up Ancestry again and helped me quite a bit in following some lines further back.

Then also HNowledge[1], a free iOS app for browsing the HN stories and comments I've upvoted. Made it to fit the way I browse HN, which is upvoting mainly what I find interesting and may want to come back to. The app lets you browse by date, domain or score, add notes and export. Apart from syncing your upvotes from HN, everything stays local without any tracking.

[1]: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hnowledge/id6813417548

Wanes[2], an Apple Health logging interface for tracking how long symptoms last. I tend to have headaches quite often and the way Apple lets you enter that data is pretty limited, so I created an app which starts a Live Activity for one or more symptoms using widgets, Control Center or Siri. You can change the severity rating while it runs and stop it from wherever you are on your phone (Home Screen, Lock Screen, Dynamic Island, Siri).

[2]: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wanes/id6811679904
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (November 2026)
